nina: Small follow-up from the device-index incident. We're seeing a related but slightly different case: scheduler packs tiny inference pods (request gpu.memory=6Gi) across multiple GPUs on a node since we allow fractional device allocations, but the device-plugin doesn't support fractional slices on newer drivers => kubelet evicts with "resource temporarily unavailable".

rajeev: Are these devices advertised as fractional-capable?

kai: No, older device-plugin advertised allowFractional=true via NodeResource, newer ones don't. Mixed state due to rolling daemonset. When scheduler sees fractional capacity it splits a pod across GPUs (e.g., 0.25 on gpu0 + 0.75 on gpu1) leading to runtime bind failure.

infra: Short fix: set `enable-fractional=false` in admission webhook for now and restart device-plugin rollout.

ops: This matches peak churn; blocking rollout mid-day helped. Cost ticket updated.

sre-bot: Eviction rate dropped 70% after taints. Keep monitoring.

nina: We'll add a scheduler validation plugin to refuse fractional allocation unless node annotation `gpu.fractional=true`. Also run a one-off job to annotate nodes correctly after device-plugin stabilizes.

rajeev: Sounds good. I filed PR #1248 for the webhook and PR #1249 for node-annotator.

ops: I'll coordinate with infra to schedule daemonset rollout during low traffic window tonight.

nina: Thanks team. We'll circle back in the PM sync.
